title: Landscape brief
description: # Landscape Brief: Prompt Caching in LLMs
content:
# Landscape Brief: Prompt Caching in LLMs

## What It Is (Core Concept)
Prompt caching is an inference optimization technique that stores intermediate **Key-Value (KV) tensor computations** from the transformer attention mechanism so they can be reused when subsequent requests share the same prompt prefix. Rather than recomputing from scratch each time, the model resumes from cached states — reducing **Time to First Token (TTFT)**, input token costs, and compute. It is *not* response caching (the model still generates fresh output).

---

## Major Sub-Areas / Themes

### 1. Mechanics & the KV Cache
The foundational mechanism is the transformer's KV cache. Prompt caching extends this to *cross-request* reuse. Key terminology: **prefill phase** (computing KV for the input), **decode phase** (autoregressive generation), **cache hit/miss**, **prefix matching**, **cache checkpoint / breakpoint**, **TTL (Time to Live)**. Sources covering the mechanics include explainers from IBM, Redis, Towards Data Science, ngrok, DigitalOcean, and MachineLearningMastery.

### 2. Prompt-Level Caching vs. Semantic Caching
A frequently contested distinction:
- **Prefix/prompt caching**: reuses KV intermediate states for exact token-level prefix matches; only saves prefill compute; output tokens are still generated.
- **Semantic caching**: stores full input→output pairs and retrieves them by embedding similarity for *similar* (not just identical) queries; bypasses LLM calls entirely on hits.
- **"Double caching"** strategy combines both layers. Tools like GPTCache and Redis vector cache support semantic caching. See BentoML's handbook and Redis blog for the comparison.

### 3. Provider Implementations
All major API providers now offer this, with different designs:
- **OpenAI**: automatic for prompts ≥1,024 tokens; 50% discount on cached input tokens; 128-token granularity increments; extended caching offloads KV to GPU-local storage (up to 24h). See official OpenAI docs and OpenAI Cookbook.
- **Anthropic (Claude)**: explicit `cache_control` parameter; developer marks cache breakpoints; TTL of 5 minutes (default) or 1 hour; up to 4 breakpoints; 90% cost reduction, 85% latency reduction claimed.
- **Google (Gemini)**: "context caching" API; explicit cache creation; TTL default 60 minutes; Gemini 2.5 adds *implicit caching*; also supported on Vertex AI.
- **AWS Bedrock**: wraps Anthropic and other models; similar reported savings.

### 4. Open-Source Serving Frameworks
- **vLLM**: Automatic Prefix Caching (APC) using block-level hashing; evicts via LRU on leaf nodes of a prefix tree. See vLLM official docs.
- **SGLang / RadixAttention**: token-level radix tree enabling irregular tree-structured sharing patterns; achieves up to 5x throughput gains vs baselines; benchmarked ~10% better than vLLM in multi-turn scenarios. See LMSYS blog and SGLang arXiv paper.

### 5. Advanced Research Directions
Academic work has pushed well beyond simple prefix matching:
- **Position-independent caching (PIC)**: chunk-level reuse at *arbitrary* positions, not just prefix (MEPIC).
- **Cross-model KV reuse**: sharing KV caches between different model variants (DroidSpeak, cross-model LoRA prefix reuse).
- **Multi-tenant / multi-agent sharing**: PolyKV, KVShare, TokenDance, KVFlow — reducing redundancy when many agents or users share common context.
- **KV cache compression + caching**: KVzip, KVTuner, WKVQuant — quantizing or evicting KV entries while preserving reusability.
- **Edge/distributed caching**: RL-based active caching at edge nodes (IEEE WCNC 2025).
- **Disaggregated serving**: CXL-based shared KV memory at rack scale (TraCT).

### 6. Prompt Structuring Best Practices
Consensus across practitioners: **"Static-first, dynamic-last."** System prompts, tool definitions, large documents, and conversation history go at the beginning; the live user query goes at the end. TTL management (5-min vs. 1-hour) is a real operational concern.

### 7. Security & Privacy
An emerging concern: **timing side-channels** in multi-tenant systems. Cache hits are observably faster than misses, allowing adversarial users to reconstruct other users' prompts via hit/miss patterns. CacheSolidarity (arXiv 2026) proposes mitigations. OpenAI notes that in-memory prompt caching doesn't impact data residency.

---

## Gaps & Under-Covered Angles
- **Accuracy impact of caching**: does KV reuse ever affect model outputs? Mostly assumed to be lossless, but cross-model or compressed-KV reuse may introduce deviations (touched on in KVShare).
- **Pricing models and economics** across providers in depth.
- **Fine-tuned / LoRA model caching**: some coverage (cross-model LoRA reuse paper), but limited.
- **Multimodal context caching** (images, audio, video): Gemini supports it; academic work is thin.

---

## Source Clusters
- **Practitioner explainers**: IBM, Redis, Towards Data Science, DigitalOcean, MachineLearningMastery, Medium
- **Industry case studies**: Thomson Reuters Labs, ProjectDiscovery, ngrok
- **Official provider docs**: Anthropic, OpenAI (API docs + Cookbook), Google AI / Vertex AI, AWS
- **Open-source framework docs**: vLLM docs, LMSYS/SGLang blog, SGLang arXiv
- **Academic papers**: arXiv / Semantic Scholar — primarily ACL, IEEE, ACM venues; heavy 2024–2026 vintage
